key_insight: PIWF splits multiscale flow representations into global Fourier modes and local wavelet features, then fuses them with physics-informed training to better capture shocks, wakes, and vortices.
engineering_relevance: This offers a practical surrogate modeling approach for fluid systems where conserving large-scale physics and resolving sharp localized structures are both critical but labeled data are scarce.
method: Fourier branch models long-range coherent, smooth flow components.
Wavelet branch captures compact, steep-gradient and vortical structures.
Residual MLP with channel attention fuses both branches under PDE, IC, and BC constraints.
evidence_signal: The method was evaluated on five canonical benchmarks—Burgers', shallow water, Kovasznay flow, Taylor-Green vortex, and 2D cylinder wake—and reported better resolution of gradients, interfaces, wake fields, vorticity extrema, and spectra than PINNs and PI-KANs.
watch_item: Wavelet-Fourier fusion and physics-informed losses can increase implementation complexity and sensitivity to branch balancing, basis selection, and training stability.
paper_title: Physics informed wavelet Fourier representation for multiscale fluid dynamics
